subtitle: When the Lion Yielded: Shivaji, Jai Singh and the Net at Purandar

panels.shot: epic split-panel wide, one half showing Shivaji on a battered hill-fort wall, the other half Jai Singh before a vast Mughal camp
panels.action: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj stands on the ramparts of Purandar, cloak whipped by the monsoon wind, facing far away towards an immense Mughal camp where the distant silhouette of Mirza Raja Jai Singh surveys lines of tents and artillery.

dialogue.text: In 1665, atop Purandar’s battered stones, Shivaji met Mirza Raja Jai Singh, a Hindu general of a Muslim emperor, and chose to bend rather than break—changing the fate of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: १६६५ में, टूटे‑फूटे पूरंदर किले पर शिवाजी ने मिर्जा राजा जयसिंह से भेंट की और टूटने की जगह झुकने का रास्ता चुना — और दक्कन की किस्मत बदल दी।

panels.shot: high aerial wide over the Deccan plateau dotted with forts
panels.action: A sweeping view of the Deccan plateau shows rocky hills capped with tiny stone forts, winding paths, scattered villages, and distant dust plumes of marching armies under a grey, humid sky.

dialogue.text: By the mid-1660s, Shivaji’s forts dotted the Deccan hills like thorns in the flesh of the Mughal Empire, pricking Aurangzeb’s pride and slowing his march south.

i18n.hi: १६६० के दशक के बीच तक शिवाजी के किले दक्कन की पहाड़ियों पर ऐसे चुभ रहे थे मानो मुग़ल सल्तनत के बदन में काँटे हों, औरंगज़ेब की शान को खरोंचते, उसके दक्षिणी क़दम धीमे करते।

panels.shot: imperial court wide in Aurangzeb’s durbar
panels.action: Inside a richly adorned Mughal hall, Aurangzeb sits austere on a low throne, nobles standing in careful ranks as a court scribe unrolls reports of Shivaji’s raids on rich caravans and coastal towns.

dialogue.text: Reports piled up in Aurangzeb’s court—burning caravans, raided ports, broken revenue chains. The Maratha chief had become more than a rebel; he was now a strategic problem.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब के दरबार में ख़बरें ढेर हो रहीं: जलते काफ़िले, लूटे बन्दरगाह, टूटी महसूली ज़ंजीरें। मराठा सरदार अब सिर्फ़ बाग़ी नहीं, एक चालाक सैन्य पहेली बन चुका था।

panels.shot: medium close on Jai Singh receiving imperial farman
panels.action: Mirza Raja Jai Singh, dignified in Rajput attire with Mughal honors, bows slightly as a farman is presented to him by a court servant in Aurangzeb’s hall, his face calm yet intent.

dialogue.text: Aurangzeb turned to Mirza Raja Jai Singh of Amber, a seasoned Rajput commander whose loyalty to the Mughal throne was matched by a cool, tactical mind.

i18n.hi: औरंगज़ेब ने आमेर के मिर्जा राजा जयसिंह को पुकारा — बूढ़ा लेकिन बाज़‑नज़र राजपूत सेनापति, जिसकी वफ़ादारी और उसकी ठंडी, सोची‑समझी चालें दोनों ही बेमिसाल थीं।

panels.shot: map-table top-down shot with hands and markers
panels.action: Over a large parchment map of the Deccan, Jai Singh’s ringed hand moves small stone markers shaped like forts and cavalry, court officers watching as he traces routes towards Purandar and the Western Ghats.

dialogue.text: Jai Singh studied the hills, the passes, the sea routes. He knew the Deccan could not be ruled by force alone; it had to be netted, knot by deliberate knot.

i18n.hi: जयसिंह ने पहाड़, दर्रे, समुद्री राहें सब तौल डालीं। वह जानता था, दक्कन सिर्फ़ तलवार से नहीं, धीरे‑धीरे बुने गए जाल से ही काबू आएगा।

panels.shot: epic wide of Mughal-Deccan army approaching Purandar
panels.action: A vast Mughal army, with artillery, war-elephants, and long lines of soldiers in mixed Rajput and Mughal attire, winds up towards a rugged hill crowned by the strong walls of Purandar fort.

dialogue.text: In early 1665, Jai Singh led a large army into the Deccan. His goal was clear: break Shivaji’s defensive ring of forts, starting with the hard rock of Purandar.

i18n.hi: १६६५ की शुरुआत में जयसिंह भारी सेना लेकर दक्कन में उतरा। उसका निशाना साफ़ था: शिवाजी के किलों की रक्षा‑अंगूठी तोड़ना, और शुरुआत करनी पूरंदर की चट्टान से।

panels.shot: medium on Shivaji on rampart watching enemy camp firelights at dusk
panels.action: Shivaji stands on the darkening ramparts of Purandar, hand resting on the stone parapet, watching thousands of tiny campfires glow in the valley below as Mughal tents spread like a white sea.

dialogue.text: From Purandar’s height, Shivaji watched the valley fill with tents and campfires. This was not a passing raid; it was the weight of the empire settling at his doorstep.

i18n.hi: पूरंदर की ऊँचाई से शिवाजी ने घाटी को तंबुओं और अलावों से भरते देखा। यह कोई छापामार हमला नहीं, खुद सल्तनत का बोझ उसकी चौखट पर आ बैठा था।

panels.shot: tight medium of Shivaji with commanders in a stone chamber
panels.action: Inside a shadowed stone chamber lit by oil lamps, Shivaji confers with a few stern Maratha commanders; maps and letters lie spread before them as they gesture towards different forts and routes.

dialogue.text: His kingdom was young, his enemies many. Old foes like Afzalkhan and Shaista Khan had fallen, but now a seasoned Rajput prince commanded imperial forces against him.

i18n.hi: उसका राज्य नया था, दुश्मन अनगिनत। अफ़ज़लख़ान, शाइस्ता ख़ाँ जैसे पुराने शिकार ढेर हो चुके थे, पर अब एक मंजा हुआ राजपूत राजकुमार बादशाही फ़ौज लेकर सामने था।

panels.shot: dynamic siege wide with cannon firing at fort walls
panels.action: Cannon smoke billows as Mughal guns fire towards Purandar’s walls; defenders move along the parapets, reinforcing battered spots, while below, siege trenches crawl closer under the summer haze.

dialogue.text: The siege tightened. Mughal artillery bit into stone, sappers crept closer, and nearby Maratha posts felt the pressure of a patient, methodical advance.

i18n.hi: घेरा कसता गया। मुग़ल तोपें पत्थर चाटने लगीं, सुरंग खोदने वाले और पास सरक आए, और आसपास के मराठा गढ़ों पर एक धीमा लेकिन न छोड़ने वाला दबाव उतर आया।

panels.shot: medium on Jai Singh in his command tent with letters
panels.action: Inside a spacious tent decorated with Rajput and Mughal motifs, Jai Singh sits at a low desk, reading reports and dictating calmly to a scribe while a map of surrounding forts hangs behind him.

dialogue.text: Jai Singh did not rely on brute force alone. He opened correspondence, sent envoys, and made it clear that submission to the emperor could preserve men and some forts.

i18n.hi: जयसिंह ने सिर्फ़ ज़बरदस्ती पर भरोसा नहीं किया। उसने ख़त लिखे, दूत भेजे और साफ़ जता दिया कि बादशाह के आगे झुकने से आदमी भी बच सकते हैं, कुछ किले भी।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of Shivaji reading a letter
panels.action: Shivaji sits cross-legged in a modest stone room, lit by a single lamp, as he reads a finely written Persian letter, his face tense, a sealing cord and broken seal resting beside him.

dialogue.text: Shivaji received Jai Singh’s terms. The language was imperial, Persian and formal, but behind the words lay a clear choice: resist and risk ruin, or yield and live to fight another day.

i18n.hi: शिवाजी के हाथ जयसिंह की शर्तें पहुँचीं। जुबान फ़ारसी, अंदाज़ बादशाही, पर पर्दे के पीछे बात सीधी थी: डटे रहो तो सर्वनाश, झुको तो कल फिर लड़ने की साँस।

panels.shot: close-up on Shivaji’s thoughtful face in half-shadow
panels.action: A close view shows Shivaji’s face half in shadow, brows knit, eyes lowered in thought, as the faint outline of the fort wall stones frames him in the background.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: Stone can be rebuilt. A people destroyed cannot.

i18n.hi: पत्थर फिर उठ खड़े हो सकते हैं, मिटा दिया गया जन कभी वापस नहीं आता।

panels.shot: low-angle of Shivaji descending from fort gateway with small escort
panels.action: Shivaji, unarmored and in simple noble attire, walks out from Purandar’s massive wooden gate with a small, composed escort, descending a stone path towards the Mughal camp in the valley.

dialogue.text: At last, Shivaji took a step few expected from him. He left the safety of his hill and walked down into the enemy’s camp to meet the emperor’s general.

i18n.hi: आख़िरकार शिवाजी ने वह क़दम उठाया जिसकी बहुतों ने उम्मीद न की थी। वह पहाड़ी सुरक्षित आसरा छोड़, नीचे दुश्मन के डेरे में उतर आया, बादशाह के सरदार से मिलने।

panels.shot: wide interior of Jai Singh’s audience tent with both figures facing each other
panels.action: Inside Jai Singh’s large audience tent, carpets laid neatly, Shivaji stands respectfully before the seated Rajput general, who looks at him with a measured, almost fatherly gaze as attendants stand back in silence.

dialogue.text: The meeting at Purandar was not between enemies of different faiths, but between two warriors of the same land, tied to different thrones and bound by their own duties.

i18n.hi: पूरंदर की मुलाक़ात दो धर्मों के दुश्मनों की नहीं, एक ही मिट्टी के दो योद्धाओं की थी — बस तख़्त अलग, फ़र्ज़ अलग।

panels.shot: medium two-shot focusing on Jai Singh speaking, Shivaji listening
panels.action: Jai Singh, hand raised in gentle emphasis, addresses Shivaji, who listens intently, hands folded, while a small brazier glows between them, casting soft light on their faces.

dialogue.text: Sources recall Jai Singh urging prudence. He spoke of the empire’s strength, of the dangers of obstinacy, and hinted at future chances within the Mughal system.

i18n.hi: कहानियाँ बताती हैं कि जयसिंह ने समझदारी का दम भरा। उसने सल्तनत की ताक़त, ज़िद की तबाही और मुग़ल ढाँचे के भीतर आने वाले मौक़ों की तरफ़ इशारा किया।

panels.shot: close on Shivaji bowing slightly with controlled humility
panels.action: Shivaji bows slightly, hands joined, his posture disciplined, as if weighing each gesture, while behind him a faint outline of Purandar’s battered silhouette can be seen through the tent opening.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: I accept the Padshah’s command, if my people may yet endure.

i18n.hi: मैं बादशाह का हुक्म मानता हूँ — अगर मेरा जन अब भी बच सके।

panels.shot: tabletop close-up of treaty document being sealed
panels.action: A parchment bearing neat Persian script lies on a low table; a Mughal official presses a seal into warm wax while another hand, with Maratha-style bracelets, rests nearby in resigned stillness.

dialogue.text: On 11 June 1665, the Treaty of Purandar was concluded. The Akhbarat records its hard terms with cool clarity.

i18n.hi: ११ जून १६६५ को पूरंदर की संधि तय हुई। अख़बारात नामे ने उसकी सख़्त शर्तें ठंडी, साफ़ ज़ुबान में दर्ज कीं।

panels.shot: montage-like wide of multiple small forts with flags lowered
panels.action: Across a wide Deccan landscape, several small hill-forts are shown in sequence, their Maratha flags being lowered as Mughal standards rise, while a few watchers stand with tightened jaws and folded arms.

dialogue.text: Shivaji agreed to surrender twenty-three forts and vast territories, keeping only twelve strongholds. Many hill crests that once flew his standard now bore imperial colors.

i18n.hi: शिवाजी ने तेईस किले और विशाल इलाक़े छोड़ने मान लिए, और सिर्फ़ बारह मज़बूत गढ़ अपने पास रखे। जिन पहाड़ियों पर कल तक उसका भगवा लहराता था, वहाँ अब शाही निशान चढ़ा।

panels.shot: medium of a young boy (symbolic Sambhaji) being presented to Mughal officer
panels.action: A young boy in fine Maratha clothes stands beside an elder as he is introduced to a Mughal officer; behind them, mounted cavalry in imperial style waits, suggesting his entry into Mughal service.

dialogue.text: He consented to send his son Sambhaji as a mansabdar, a ranked officer in Mughal service, and acknowledged the emperor’s suzerainty over his remaining lands.

i18n.hi: उसने अपने बेटे संभाजी को मुग़ल सेवा में मनसबदार भेजने की हामी भरी और अपनी बाक़ी ज़मीनों पर बादशाह की बड़हक़ूमी मान ली।

panels.shot: dim study shot of a scribe writing Persian letter by lamplight
panels.action: In a quiet room, a scribe writes flowing Persian lines by lamplight as another figure dictates in the background, scrolls piled neatly nearby, conveying the preparation of formal letters.

dialogue.text: Shivaji’s letters to Aurangzeb, composed in courtly Persian, adopt a tone of deep submission, describing himself as a humble servant seeking the emperor’s pardon.

i18n.hi: शिवाजी के औरंगज़ेब को लिखे ख़त, नफ़ीस फ़ारसी में, गहरी आज़रदस्ती दिखाते हैं — वह अपने को ताबेदार, गुनहगार, बादशाह की माफ़ी माँगता ख़ादिम बताता है।

panels.shot: close on Shivaji’s hand resting firmly on a Persian letter
panels.action: Shivaji’s hand presses flat on an unrolled letter bearing ornate Persian script, his fingers steady, while his face, partly visible, shows controlled resolve rather than despair.

dialogue.text: To some, those words seem uncharacteristically meek. But the letters show a man using the empire’s own language to buy space and time in a moment of peril.

i18n.hi: कुछ को ये लफ़्ज़ शिवाजी के लिए अजीब‑से नरम लगते हैं। पर ये चिट्ठियाँ एक ऐसे आदमी को दिखाती हैं जो ख़तरे की घड़ी में सल्तनत की ज़ुबान से ही अपने लिए वक़्त और जगह खरीद रहा था।

panels.shot: wide of Aurangzeb’s court again, officer reading letter aloud
panels.action: Back in Aurangzeb’s hall, a court official reads aloud from a letter while Aurangzeb listens, expression inscrutable, nobles leaning in slightly as the words of Shivaji’s humble address echo in the chamber.

dialogue.text: In Delhi, these letters reinforced Aurangzeb’s sense of victory. Here was the once-defiant hill chief accepting the titles and framework of the Mughal order.

i18n.hi: दिल्ली में इन ख़तों ने औरंगज़ेब को और फूला दिया। पहाड़ी बाग़ी अब वही मुग़ल ओहदे और ढाँचे कुबूल कर रहा था जिनके ख़िलाफ़ वह कल तक अड़ा था।

panels.shot: medium of Jai Singh and Shivaji together overlooking map of Deccan
panels.action: In a calmer moment, Jai Singh and Shivaji stand side by side over a spread map, Jai Singh pointing towards the north while Shivaji listens, the tent walls now quiet around them.

dialogue.text: Jai Singh pressed further, urging Shivaji to join imperial campaigns in the south. He imagined the Maratha as a valuable ally within, not outside, the Mughal net.

i18n.hi: जयसिंह यहीं नहीं रुका। उसने शिवाजी को दक्षिण की बादशाही मुहिमों में शामिल होने को उकसाया — वह मराठा को जाल के बाहर नहीं, भीतर एक कीमती साथी के रूप में देखना चाहता था।

panels.shot: medium on Shivaji mounting a horse in Mughal camp, with mixed feelings
panels.action: In the Mughal camp, Shivaji mounts a horse amid imperial troops preparing to march, his face composed but distant, as Rajput and Mughal officers watch this new ally join their column.

dialogue.text: For a brief time, Shivaji moved within Jai Singh’s net, accompanying the Mughal general on campaigns, outwardly a loyal subordinate of the empire he had long defied.

i18n.hi: कुछ समय को शिवाजी, जयसिंह के जाल के भीतर ही चला — मुग़ल सरदार के साथ मुहिमों में गया, ऊपर से पूरा वफ़ादार, उसी सल्तनत का जो हमेशा से उसकी दुश्मन रही थी।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of Shivaji riding, distant southern hills ahead
panels.action: Shivaji rides at the edge of a marching column, the southern hills hazy ahead, his gaze turned sideways towards the distant Western Ghats rather than the road in front.

dialogue.speaker: chhatrapati_shivaji_maharaj
dialogue.text: A trapped bird learns the pattern of the cage.

i18n.hi: फँसा पक्षी पिंजरे की हर डंडी गिनना सीख जाता है।

panels.shot: symbolic wide of a net spread over a small hill-fort model
panels.action: On a plain surface, a detailed miniature of a hill-fort sits under a fine rope net being gently drawn tight by two unseen hands from opposite sides, suggesting control without visible violence.

dialogue.text: Jai Singh’s strategy combined siege, diplomacy and honor. His net at Purandar did not rely on massacre, but on binding a dangerous foe into imperial service.

i18n.hi: जयसिंह की चाल घेराबंदी, सियासत और इज़्ज़त का मेल थी। पूरंदर का उसका जाल कत्लेआम पर नहीं, दुश्मन को ही बादशाही सेवा की रस्सियों से बाँधने पर टिका था।

panels.shot: melancholic wide of Maratha villagers watching fort under new flag
panels.action: Villagers stand at the edge of a field, looking up at a fort where a Mughal standard now flies; some point, others stand quietly, oxen and carts nearby, as clouds gather overhead.

dialogue.text: For the people below the forts, the change was immediate yet subtle. New flags, new officers, but the same hills, the same fields, the same hope that war might pass them by.

i18n.hi: किलों के नीचे रहने वालों के लिए बदलाव तुरत भी था, हल्का भी। झंडे बदले, अफ़सर बदले, पर वही पहाड़, वही खेत, वही उम्मीद कि शायद अब जंग उनसे दूर गुज़र जाए।

panels.shot: introspective medium of Shivaji back in a modest chamber, no armor
panels.action: Later, Shivaji sits alone in a modest chamber, without armor or weapons, gazing at a small model fort on the floor, its flag removed, as lamplight flickers against bare stone walls.

dialogue.text: Historians caution us: Shivaji could not see the future from Purandar. He knew only that open defiance then risked the annihilation of his fragile power.

i18n.hi: इतिहासकार टोकते हैं: पूरंदर पर खड़ा शिवाजी भविष्य नहीं देख सकता था। उसे बस इतना दिखता था कि उस घड़ी की खुली बग़ावत उसकी नाज़ुक ताक़त को जड़ से उखाड़ सकती है।

panels.shot: composite wide showing later Maratha resurgence faintly in background
panels.action: In a subtle composite, the foreground shows a surrendered fort under Mughal colors, while in the faded background another fort in later years bears a revived Maratha flag, suggesting eventual resurgence without detailing it.

dialogue.text: Yet the years that followed showed how vital this pause was. Without the loss and humiliation of Purandar, there might never have been the later flowering of Maratha power.

i18n.hi: लेकिन आने वाले सालों ने दिखाया, यह ठहराव कितना ज़रूरी था। पूरंदर की हार और बेइज़्ज़ती के बिना शायद कभी आगे चलकर मराठा ताक़त की वह बड़ी लहर उठ ही न पाती।

panels.shot: final reflective shot of empty, weathered stones of Purandar at sunset
panels.action: The ancient walls of Purandar stand silent at sunset, their stones weathered but firm, the land below stretching out in soft light as a lone bird circles above the ramparts.

dialogue.text: Purandar reminds us that courage is not only a sword drawn in defiance; sometimes it is the hard, quiet act of yielding in order to outlive a stronger enemy and fight for another dawn.

i18n.hi: पूरंदर याद दिलाता है कि वीरता हमेशा तलवार खींचकर गरजने में नहीं; कई बार यह चुप, कठोर निर्णय में छिपी होती है — झुकने की, बस इतना जीने की कि कल फिर उठकर मज़बूत दुश्मन से जंग की जा सके।

title_i18n.en: Purandar Treaty and Jai Singh's Net
